Codex review: blocked before merge. ## What this changes This PR adapts legacy database fingerprints inside candidate Doctor and prepares schemas and cron identity for direct extended-stable upgrades. **Example:** Update an installation running OpenClaw 2026.9.34 directly to a candidate containing this repair. - **Before:** Candidate Doctor can reject unchanged databases with “SQLite migration source changed after update capture.” - **After:** Doctor verifies the legacy inventory, attributes migrations using committed generations, and returns fingerprints the installed updater understands. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | The compatibility repair has clear value and meaningful boundary coverage, but an introduced test fails and persisted-state upgrade acceptance remains incomplete. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | The ordinary contributor media gate does not apply to this maintainer-authored PR; the body supplies focused regression results but explicitly claims no final-candidate product PASS. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** An extended-stable installation can pass rehearsal but fail actual upgrade because Doctor rejects unchanged captured databases. **Reason:** Compatibility with a shipped updater is a concrete product requirement, and the maintainer-authored direction is already approved. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 2 items remain** Keep open: this maintainer-authored PR addresses a documented shipped-updater incompatibility, but its newly added explicit-config cron regression fails on the reviewed head. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `e5f6d0f2eec82cc109d55a5dc9689b7cd10a649f` ## Before merge - [ ] **Fix the added explicit-config cron snapshot case (P2)** - The newly added `explicit config` case fails on this exact head in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11`: it supplies a config-directory selector and expects `config/cron/jobs.json`, but the reopened copy selects `source/cron/jobs.json`. This leaves the PR's claimed explicit-selector preservation unverified and introduces a failing CI test. Correct the fixture/input or projection according to the existing selector contract, preserving the assertion that the intended partition survives. - [ ] **Add data-model compatibility proof** - The review found that existing stored data may not work after upgrade. Show that existing data still loads and works with this change. ## Findings - [P2] Fix the added explicit-config cron snapshot case — `src/infra/update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts:347-348` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: Final-candidate direct extended-stable upgrade, latest-stable upgrade, and forced rollback acceptance with retained settings and data are not demonstrated.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The installed updater supplies captured database generations to candidate Doctor, which migrates preserved state and returns write receipts for rollback verification. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Installed updater] --> B[Captured legacy inventory] B --> C[Candidate Doctor] C --> D[Paired generation observation] D --> E[Existing schema migration owners] E --> F[Settled legacy receipt] F --> G[Rollback verification] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Retain candidate-side normalization in the existing owners and correct the explicit-config cron regression without weakening partition-selection checks. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Released 2026.9.34 and current main use incompatible fingerprint formats, corroborated by native failures recorded in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179349; this review executed no target code. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Whole-inventory verification followed by candidate-local normalization addresses the compatibility boundary while retaining current generation and migration owners. Full review comments: - [P2] Fix the added explicit-config cron snapshot case — `src/infra/update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts:347-348` The newly added `explicit config` case fails on this exact head in `checks-node-changed-compact-small-11`: it supplies a config-directory selector and expects `config/cron/jobs.json`, but the reopened copy selects `source/cron/jobs.json`. This leaves the PR's claimed explicit-selector preservation unverified and introduces a failing CI test. Correct the fixture/input or projection according to the existing selector contract, preserving the assertion that the intended partition survives. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.88 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [7b95dbd3fdfe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b95dbd3fdfe7faafdda0a68e31cf8a304c00cff). ### Provenance checked - `Committed versus physical database generations` keeps the original intent (0ac1c241fba8cb0e255a907e5f23e523ec579a43: Committed-content fingerprints replaced physical fingerprints so checkpoint-only changes would not prevent safe rollback.) - `Migration and native-close attribution` keeps the original intent (8f622108e0003e722801b420187b6011e0a4536e: Credential cutover retained source-bound migration receipts and native custody for exact recovery.) - `Version preparation before broader maintenance` keeps the original intent (3cd9950c462b4cf4bd56becf5517f14adbfc574e: Declared version phases finish before broader repairs so scoped backups retain their defined recovery boundary.) - `Empty-reader WAL-index equivalence` keeps the original intent (237fdc662d90d216a8693fa6b9178afc0cbc54d6: A zero-write WAL index may appear or disappear after a read-only probe without changing committed contents.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - pnpm test src/infra/update-candidate-state.inventory.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - pnpm test src/infra/update-doctor-migration-attribution.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - git diff --check What I checked: - **Pinned introduced change:** Reviewed the merge-base-to-head diff; the adapter remains in candidate inspection and Doctor settlement, without introducing configuration, dependencies, or another durable store. ([`src/infra/update-doctor-result.ts:297`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/e5f6d0f2eec82cc109d55a5dc9689b7cd10a649f/src/infra/update-doctor-result.ts#L297), [e5f6d0f2eec8](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/e5f6d0f2eec82cc109d55a5dc9689b7cd10a649f)) - **Verified released fingerprint contract:** Published v2026.9.34 hashes serialized physical file generations and the 96-byte WAL-index header; the added physical observation reproduces that contract. ([`src/infra/update-database-generations.ts`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/f123d430a7dea78c9d78e05606c4cad621c0e2c8/src/infra/update-database-generations.ts), [f123d430a7de](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/f123d430a7dea78c9d78e05606c4cad621c0e2c8)) - **Current main still needs compatibility:** Fetched main retains committed-content generations without legacy inventory normalization; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/179349 records native failures and credits the verified intermediate-upgrade workaround. ([`src/infra/update-database-generations.ts:140`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/7b95dbd3fdfe7faafdda0a68e31cf8a304c00cff/src/infra/update-database-generations.ts#L140), [7b95dbd3fdfe](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/7b95dbd3fdfe7faafdda0a68e31cf8a304c00cff)) - **Introduced cron regression fails:** The exact-head CI annotation reports that the new explicit-config case expected config/cron/jobs.json but received source/cron/jobs.json: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40312346871/job/121537003203.
